expectations.text: Acknowledges that node selection is a substantive theoretical choice, not a neutral one, and that network structure depends on which items are included
expectations.evidence: "The nodes you choose *are* the theory. Choosing Y-BOCS items is choosing to model OCD as a system of severity facets, and that choice needs to be owned and defended rather than treated as a neutral data-collection decision." Also: "the network approach is not a method you apply to *any* item set and read off disorder structure."

expectations.text: References Fried's work on node selection, depression symptom heterogeneity, or the 'What are good depression symptoms' / '52 symptoms' line of work — OR makes the equivalent substantive point without the citation
expectations.evidence: "The canonical references the reviewer is implicitly invoking are Fried (2017, *J Affect Disorders*, 'The 52 symptoms of major depression') and Fried, Epskamp, Nesse, Tuerlinckx & Borsboom (2016) 'What are good depression symptoms?' Both argue that node selection is a theoretical act with large consequences for estimated network structure."

expectations.text: Mentions node redundancy / topological overlap as a methodological concern (near-duplicate items inflate edge weights)
expectations.evidence: "These pairs may produce strong edges not because the underlying phenomena causally interact but because they are functionally near-duplicate items with nearly identical conditioning sets." The response explicitly flags the parallel obsession/compulsion item structure as a redundancy concern that distorts edge weights.

expectations.text: Suggests checking for redundant nodes (e.g., networktools, goldbricker) or justifying selection theoretically
expectations.evidence: "Run `networktools::goldbricker(data)` before estimation — you may find several flagged pairs." Also in the reviewer response section: "Report goldbricker results to demonstrate you checked for node redundancy."
